title: A real-time distributed architecture for large-scale tactile sensing
authors: E. Baglini, S. Youssefi, F. Mastrogiovanni and G. Cannata
read_scope: Official IROS2014 digest, p.134, and author-uploaded abstract; original seven-page paper not obtained.
finding: Describes an EtherCAT-based distributed network connecting computational nodes associated with skin patches and evaluates the real-time architecture.
limitation: The accessible material does not establish the exact hardware cost, measured deadline distribution, or fault containment available to this project. EtherCAT results cannot certify a CAN FD implementation.
plan_action: Adapt its separation of local acquisition, transport and host processing. Keep CAN FD for the low-cost baseline; qualify deadlines under maximum traffic before increasing node count.
test: Timestamp ADC scan completion, CAN transmission, gateway reception and consumer execution separately. Test every region at maximum active traffic while logging, displaying data and injecting node resets.
novelty: Distributed patch processing and real-time tactile networking are established prior art.

title: A real-time data acquisition and processing framework for large-scale robot skin
authors: S. Youssefi, S. Denei, F. Mastrogiovanni and G. Cannata
read_scope: Publisher-indexed introduction and selected architecture/implementation sections, including Skinware abstraction and historical test platform. Full results and figures not reviewed.
finding: Skinware separates tactile applications from particular sensors and network technologies and treats data coherence, consistency and timing as architectural concerns. Its reported environment includes RTAI and an older Linux platform.
limitation: Historical software-platform results do not establish present ROS2/Linux deadline behavior or direct STM32/CAN compatibility.
plan_action: Adopt immutable complete-scan snapshots with versioned metadata and bounded producer-consumer queues. Keep real-time consumers independent from visualization, file I/O and discovery.
test: Freeze or crash the UI/logger while exercising acquisition. Assert the control consumer sees either a coherent fresh snapshot or an explicit invalid/stale state, never a mixture of scans.
novelty: A common sensor abstraction and real-time skin middleware are established; contribution must be reproducible integration quality and cost.

title: Asynchronous, event-driven readout of POSFET devices for tactile sensing
authors: S. Caviglia, M. Valle and C. Bartolozzi
read_scope: Identity and conference pages2648–2651 checked against ISCAS proceedings contents; original abstract/body not obtained. DOI corroborated by later scholarly reference lists.
finding: The title establishes an earlier POSFET/event-readout line of work. No device-level performance or circuit claim from this paper is relied upon here.
limitation: No original circuit schematic, process, power, noise or bandwidth was available for audit; a POSFET circuit cannot be presumed equivalent to the chosen resistive film.
plan_action: Do not transplant or cost a POSFET circuit from this citation. The baseline continues to use a conventional ADC and firmware change detection; identify that as sampled event reporting.
test: Document actual scan period and first-sample latency. Do not label the MCU design a continuously asynchronous transducer.
novelty: The title is enough to flag asynchronous tactile readout as pre-existing work; performance comparison requires the original paper.

title: Event-driven encoding of off-the-shelf tactile sensors for compression and latency optimisation for robotic skin
authors: C. Bartolozzi et al.
read_scope: Author-uploaded manuscript excerpts: architecture, encoding comparison and conclusions. Primary IIT laboratory publication listing also checked. Full paper was not independently downloaded.
finding: Studies event encodings of existing tactile sensors, including recorded iCub fingertip data, and describes an FPGA-based acquisition path with hierarchical event addressing. Sensor conversion and event transport are distinct stages.
limitation: Fingertip datasets, FPGA acquisition and AS-AER links do not demonstrate whole-limb resistive-film performance. Encoding simulations and hardware properties must be distinguished.
plan_action: Adopt explicit body/patch/site identifiers, acquisition timestamps and a reproducible raw-data-versus-event comparison. Keep CAN integrity and periodic absolute snapshots; reject an FPGA hub as the minimum-cost baseline.
test: Replay identical raw recordings through periodic and hybrid encoders. Report event onset misses, absolute reconstruction error, bytes on the wire and end-to-end age, including packet overhead.
novelty: Off-the-shelf tactile event conversion, address hierarchies and event compression are prior art.

title: The event-driven software library for YARP—With algorithms and iCub applications
authors: A. Glover, V. Vasco, M. Iacono and C. Bartolozzi
read_scope: Publisher-indexed sections3.2–3.3 on event representation, readers/queues and processing; complete article body not retrieved.
finding: Provides event packet representations and software handling in YARP, with processing decoupled from receipt. The discussion recognizes large variations in event traffic and computation.
limitation: Its illustrative large-rate examples concern vision. A flexible event library does not establish a hard skin-control deadline or justify silently skipping required control updates.
plan_action: Adapt recording/replay, typed event records and independent receive/processing threads. Use bounded queues with counters and an explicit overload state; make GUI frame dropping independent of tactile validity.
test: Burst all sites simultaneously, pause each consumer, then resume. Verify bounded memory, monotonically sequenced records and deterministic stale-data handling.
novelty: Event middleware and replay are established infrastructure; do not market them as a new sensory nervous system.

title: Humanoid multimodal tactile-sensing modules
authors: P. Mittendorfer and G. Cheng
read_scope: University bibliographic record and abstract; full methods, circuit and characterization tables not obtained.
finding: Describes modular off-the-shelf multimodal skin with local digitization/processing and network connectivity, including temperature, acceleration and proximity sensing.
limitation: This earlier hardware generation should not be conflated with the later force-cap version. Its multimodal capability is absent from a pressure-plus-NTC patch.
plan_action: Adopt local processing and replaceable modules. Publish an explicit modality table: approximate normal contact and two temperature points in baseline; no shear, proximity or inertial self-localization.
test: For every advertised modality, demonstrate a repeatable stimulus, calibration, uncertainty and fault response using the actual production-intent patch.
novelty: Modular multimodal cells and local intelligence existed by2011.

title: Integrating discrete force cells into multi-modal artificial skin
authors: P. Mittendorfer and G. Cheng
read_scope: Repository-indexed first-page abstract, force-cell construction and introduction. Full force/displacement graphs and durability results not reviewed.
finding: Uses etched CuBe2 spring structures with capacitive measurement, three force cells per skin module, and automated assembly concepts. The paper reports2.5kHz acquisition filtered to250Hz and SNR greater than50dB.
limitation: These figures belong to a metal-spring capacitive transducer, not a printed resistive taxel. Encapsulation and mechanical preload affect performance. CuBe processing is not proposed for the home-lab film route.
plan_action: Adopt mechanical overload stops, controlled preload and a cover-specific calibration record. Reject copying its performance numbers or force-cell BOM into the resistive design.
test: Calibrate each finished cover/sensor/carrier stack, repeat after remounting and after overload, and measure loading/unloading hysteresis and zero drift.
novelty: Protected multimodal force cells and assembly-oriented mechanics are prior art.

title: Towards autonomous robotic skin spatial calibration: A framework based on vision and self-touch
authors: A. Albini, S. Denei and G. Cannata
read_scope: Primary university publication list verifies identity; a secondary abstract describes RGB-D/self-touch, but original abstract/body was not obtained. The secondary <2mm result is deliberately not adopted as validated evidence.
finding: This is relevant prior art for spatial calibration using vision and robot-generated contacts; no exact original algorithm or performance claim is used in the design.
limitation: Reachability, camera calibration, occlusion and force-distributed contact centroids need examination before reproduction. The source available here is insufficient to promise its accuracy.
plan_action: Keep registered CAD carriers as the baseline. Use external probing at marked sites as a measurable manufacturing check; describe any future vision/self-touch implementation as a separate reproduction.
test: Blindly probe predeclared site centers in several poses and report position and normal errors against the fixture geometry, rather than only fitting error.
novelty: Vision-assisted and self-touch spatial registration are not a new claim for this project.

title: 3D surface reconstruction for robotic body parts with artificial skins
authors: P. Mittendorfer and G. Cheng
read_scope: Repository first-page abstract/introduction and university abstract. The supplied2019 review §II-C supplies additional secondary explanation of reconstruction.
finding: Reconstruction uses the modular skin's known structural geometry and motion-related sensing. The approach concerns shaped, connected modules rather than an arbitrary uninstrumented stretchable sheet.
limitation: A shared CAN address list does not reveal physical adjacency; resistive touch values do not supply gravity vectors. Stretch and slip violate a fixed module geometry assumption.
plan_action: Adopt a versioned body map with per-site position and unit normal derived from the rigid carrier. Bind map revision to the installed carrier and reject unknown revisions.
test: Check normals at curved-edge sites as well as patch centers. Remount and probe several positions; inhibit control if the carrier cannot be registered within the declared tolerance.
novelty: Automatic surface reconstruction from instrumented skin is existing work, but is not implemented by the baseline BOM.

title: Open-loop self-calibration of articulated robots with artificial skins
authors: P. Mittendorfer and G. Cheng
read_scope: Repository-indexed pages1–2 including algorithms1–2, requirements and experimental/simulation scope; university abstract read directly. Full numerical results not obtained.
finding: Uses tri-axis accelerometers and isolated joint excitation to find segment/joint activity and construct kinematic models. Requires instrumented rigid segments and a static reference. Physical KUKA results establish structural exploration; parameter estimation is additionally demonstrated in simulation.
limitation: Does not validate autonomous geometry from pressure-only skin. Weak excitation, reference motion and unobserved degrees of freedom can make identification ambiguous. Full numerical error bounds were not inspected.
plan_action: Adapt activity-matrix validation using a reusable stationary-reference/downstream IMU fixture and known joint states. Retain CAD geometry; label the fixture an adaptation, not a full reproduction of autonomous skin localization.
test: Use one joint at a time; repeat with reversed motion and held-out poses. Compare detected influence with the robot kinematic tree and reject low-SNR or inconsistent results.
novelty: Activity matrices, motor excitation and accelerometer-based structural self-calibration are prior art.

title: Automatic robot kinematic modeling with a modular artificial skin
authors: P. Mittendorfer, E. Dean and G. Cheng
read_scope: University abstract and bibliographic record read directly. Original six-page article unavailable. Supplied2019 review §II-D is secondary evidence for axis/SVD/radius sequence.
finding: Uses per-cell tri-axis accelerometers, open-loop motions and circle-point analysis to build a forward kinematic model. The abstract reports a physical UR5 experiment on an inertial dual-arm platform.
limitation: No original numerical errors, conditioning tests or implementation parameters were accessible. One revolute motion identifies perpendicular radius, not the axial component of a sensor offset; full geometry needs additional constraints.
plan_action: Use axis/perpendicular-radius estimation only as an offline cross-check against CAD. Do not claim recovery of every DH offset, mass, inertia or friction from a dual-IMU experiment.
test: Fit acceleration versus known angular acceleration, retain confidence intervals and residuals, and validate against independent measured radii and unseen poses. Reject rank-deficient fits.
novelty: Automatic kinematic modeling from skin acceleration precedes this project. A low-cost reusable fixture may be an implementation distinction, subject to measurement.
bibliographic_note: Humanoids2014 proceedings; university record lists publication12Feb2015. Both dates refer to the same paper.

title: 3D spatial self-organization of a modular artificial skin
authors: P. Mittendorfer, E. Dean and G. Cheng
read_scope: Primary university abstract and identity. Full equations and numerical experiments not obtained.
finding: Combines skin-patch geometry with an active LED visual marker and a calibrated monocular camera for spatial registration, including partial visibility.
limitation: Self-organization here is not entirely camera-free. A pressure-only film lacks the per-cell inertial and active-marker information of the studied system.
plan_action: Maintain a declared manual/CAD root transform. If camera registration is used in a fixture, make camera intrinsics, marker geometry and observation quality part of its calibration record.
test: Register from several independent views; probe points withheld from the transform fit and verify the transform direction and units.
novelty: Camera-assisted skin registration is prior art; baseline simplicity is a cost/design choice, not a discovery.

title: Touch, in Principles of Neural Science, fifth edition, chapter23
authors: E. P. Gardner and K. O. Johnson
read_scope: User-supplied2019 bibliography identifies chapter23, pp.498–529. Full chapter not obtained; publisher book URL is a locator, not a claim of chapter access.
finding: Biological background cited by the2019 review. No receptor count, frequency range or quantitative biological claim is extracted here without the original chapter.
limitation: A biological analogy cannot establish robot sensitivity, safety, durability or wiring requirements.
plan_action: Describe the design as functionally inspired by distributed sensing. Preserve persistent contact state and temperature measurements; avoid claiming replication of human skin's complete receptor system.
test: Maintain a held contact for at least60s and verify it never disappears merely because signal change becomes small. Measure drift separately from valid sustained contact.
novelty: Distributed sensing inspired by skin is a long-established concept.

title: Touch is a team effort: Interplay of submodalities in cutaneous sensibility
authors: H. P. Saal and S. J. Bensmaia
read_scope: Original article abstract indexed by PubMed; full review body not obtained.
finding: The review emphasizes joint contributions of afferent submodalities to natural touch, rather than a simple one-receptor/one-percept correspondence.
limitation: It does not show that two engineered layers or sparse thermal sensors reproduce the capabilities of human skin.
plan_action: Keep claims modality-specific. Fuse contact and temperature at the application layer without implying that sparse NTC readings provide a complete thermal image or that normal pressure measures shear.
test: Test thermal drift during contact and heat without contact. Report each modality's spatial sampling, temporal response and cross-sensitivity separately.
novelty: Biological multimodal integration is motivation, not an invention claim for a pressure/temperature laminate.

title: Event-based signaling for reducing required data rates and processing power in a large-scale artificial robotic skin
authors: F. Bergner, P. Mittendorfer, E. Dean-Leon and G. Cheng
read_scope: Repository-indexed results page6, figures7–8/table/conclusion, plus official conference abstract. Whole methods not retrieved.
finding: A260-cell UR5 study reports remaining traffic of16.45% at rest and47.69% under heavy stimulation without timestamps; with timestamps,21.38% and62%. Compact packets of three events suit the correlated modalities studied.
limitation: These are remaining-traffic fractions, not reduction percentages. Packet format, timestamps and workload matter. The baseline's64-byte absolute CAN frames will not inherit these reductions.
plan_action: Use this as a benchmark design, not a promised percentage. Specify maximum50% idle snapshot-count reduction for100Hzactive/50Hzidle, with smaller total savings after extra overhead.
test: Run quiet, motor-moving, stroking, impact and simultaneous-contact workloads. Count complete wire traffic and CPU time, not only useful sensor bytes.
novelty: Local send-on-change for large robot skin and compression benchmarks are prior art.

title: Event-based signaling for large-scale artificial robotic skin—Realization and performance evaluation
authors: F. Bergner, E. Dean-Leon and G. Cheng
read_scope: Repository-indexed introduction/architecture and primary university abstract; complete experiment methods not accessed.
finding: Uses two260-cell patches with local processing. The abstract reports48.2% packet and17.79% CPU reductions in reactive control; a worst-case5000-cell extrapolation gives21.2% and17.46%, respectively.
limitation: The5000-cell result is an extrapolation, not a physical5000-cell validation. Traffic, CPU and control-rate metrics are different quantities.
plan_action: Keep a periodic diagnostic mode and a hybrid event mode in the same firmware for controlled comparison. Publish measured patch count and extrapolated counts separately.
test: Replay identical captures in both modes with the same host code. Measure CPU, latency, dropped samples and reconstruction error at1,8 and multiple independent regions.
novelty: Switchable periodic/event skin operation and performance comparisons were already demonstrated.

title: Efficient event-driven reactive control for large scale robot skin
authors: F. Bergner, E. Dean-Leon and G. Cheng
read_scope: Repository first-page abstract/introduction. Detailed control proofs and full experimental plots not accessed.
finding: Evaluates event-driven reactive control on TOMM with two253-cell patches. The abstract reports controller CPU reductions of78% idle and66% during contact relative to the tested synchronous reference.
limitation: Controller savings cannot be substituted for network or driver savings. Unchanged pressure does not imply unchanged joint torque when robot configuration changes.
plan_action: Cache contact information or link-frame wrench contributions, but recompute their mapping with current joint states in a bounded controller cycle. Separate event receipt from command execution.
test: Hold one contact steady while changing joint pose in simulation. Compare event-mode joint torques against a fully recomputed periodic reference, including stale/missing frames.
novelty: Event-driven reactive control is prior art; the project's value must lie in verified affordability and integration.

title: A128×128120dB15µs latency asynchronous temporal contrast vision sensor
authors: P. Lichtsteiner, C. Posch and T. Delbruck
read_scope: Original journal-paper reproduction, concluding page575 and indexed abstract. The reproduction is on a secondary host; full article not retrieved.
finding: A custom asynchronous contrast imager reports120dB dynamic range,15µs latency and23mW power. Its discussion identifies event-bandwidth limitations and lack of direct DC response.
limitation: These are optical custom-silicon results under the paper's conditions. They do not establish response time, energy or resolution for a scanned tactile array.
plan_action: Use only as historical distinction between truly asynchronous transduction and100Hz sampled send-on-delta. Retain absolute contact samples so static loads remain observable.
test: Measure tactile latency with a stimulus reference and oscilloscope; never infer it from the event-camera title.
novelty: Custom event sensors and address-event transmission have decades of prior art.

title: An asynchronous time-based image sensor
authors: C. Posch, D. Matolin and R. Wohlgenannt
read_scope: Primary institutional bibliographic metadata checked. A secondary abstract was found, but no original body or complete primary abstract was reviewed.
finding: Identified as prior work on asynchronous time-based optical sensing. No quantitative device claim is adopted.
limitation: It is an image-sensor design, not a tactile transducer or low-cost STM32 reference circuit.
plan_action: Do not add custom timing-coded hardware to the baseline on this citation alone. Ordinary absolute ADC values plus timestamps are sufficient for the intended touch task.
test: Document acquisition instant separately from packet arrival and verify that changing event encoding does not change the underlying sampling limit.
novelty: Time-based event representations are established and are not a defensible novel claim here.

title: AER EAR: A matched silicon cochlea pair with address event representation interface
authors: A. van Schaik and S.-C. Liu
read_scope: Primary institutional abstract. This is the2005conference paper, not the later similarly named journal work.
finding: Describes paired silicon cochleae, inner-hair-cell/spiking-neuron circuitry and address-event output; its experiment uses tones from different directions.
limitation: An auditory analog front end offers no directly transferable tactile resolution, component price or contact-safety guarantee.
plan_action: Use it as a historical example of modality-specific local event generation. Keep pressure and temperature acquisition parameters independently specified.
test: Verify both modalities retain correct physical units, sampling schedules and invalid-data flags when packed into shared transport.
novelty: Neuromorphic sensory event coding predates this project.

title: VLSI analogs of neuronal visual processing: A synthesis of form and function
authors: M. Mahowald
read_scope: Caltech thesis repository metadata and abstract. The full thesis was located but not read.
finding: Develops analog VLSI visual processing and communication inspired by neural systems, including retina/stereo/optic-nerve concepts.
limitation: A thesis abstract cannot support detailed circuit reproduction or performance comparison. Visual neuromorphic circuitry does not specify the mechanics of electronic skin.
plan_action: Cite as historical context if using the artificial-nervous-system analogy. Keep the engineering argument based on tested latency, reliability, mass and cost.
test: Audit the article's novelty claims against documented prior art and distinguish implementation economics from a new sensory-computing principle.
novelty: Neural-inspired distributed sensing and event communication are longstanding.

title: Point-to-point connectivity between neuromorphic chips using address events
authors: K. A. Boahen
read_scope: Author-hosted abstract and repository-indexed discussion/arbiter figures; not all19journal pages.
finding: Analyzes address-event communication and arbitration for time-multiplexed neuromorphic connections. Queueing and contention affect event timing and throughput.
limitation: AER timing properties do not remove finite bandwidth, arbitration delay or buffer limits, and do not automatically apply to CAN FD.
plan_action: Adopt worst-case burst and queue analysis. Preserve acquisition timestamps and distinguish age at sampling from transport delay; report queue overflow as invalid coverage.
test: Align maximum-rate reports from every node and inject retransmissions. Measure worst observed age and overflow behavior, not merely mean latency.
novelty: Sparse addresses and asynchronous arbitration are prior art.

title: Asynchronous DC-free serial protocol for event-based AER systems
authors: P. M. Ros, M. Crepaldi, C. Bartolozzi and D. Demarchi
read_scope: Primary university abstract; original article file is restricted and was not requested from authors.
finding: Proposes a serial event protocol with100Mbps raw rate and up to2.9million32-bit events/s; its abstract reports successful16-bit operation with ±2% clock mismatch, explicit flow control and AC-coupling compatibility.
limitation: These figures refer to that protocol and implementation. A differential pair does not make it electrically or logically interchangeable with CAN.
plan_action: Retain CAN FD transceivers, arbitration, error detection and diagnostics. Consider AS-AER only after a measured bandwidth bottleneck justifies separate FPGA/PHY cost.
test: Validate the actual CAN line, termination, bit timing and error recovery. Never substitute AS-AER bitrates into the CAN capacity calculation.
novelty: Serial event transport over a small wire count is already established.

title: A QVGA143dB dynamic range frame-free PWM image sensor with lossless pixel-level video compression and time-domain CDS
authors: C. Posch, D. Matolin and R. Wohlgenannt
read_scope: IEEE title/record and primary AIT institutional identity; original methods and figures not obtained. Similar2010ISSCC conference versions are not substituted.
finding: Identifies prior work on frame-free optical sensing with time-domain encoding; no numerical claim beyond the bibliographic title is adopted as engineering evidence.
limitation: The2019 review's use as an example of absolute-value event coding does not make its optical circuit an appropriate tactile design.
plan_action: Carry absolute values in the MCU frames; do not integrate received signed increments as the only persistent contact state.
test: Drop a contact-onset packet and confirm a subsequent absolute snapshot restores the current state. Also report that the missed transient itself cannot be reconstructed.
novelty: Absolute-value/time-coded event sensing is not new.

title: A new protocol for a low power sensor network
authors: M. Neugebauer and K. Kabitzsch
read_scope: Author-uploaded abstract and official conference contents; original protocol details and results not read.
finding: Discusses event-oriented activity for battery-powered sensor networks, relating communication scheduling to energy consumption.
limitation: Energy benefits depend on the radio, duty cycle and application. A wired sensor that continues sampling at100Hz does not save ADC/MCU power simply because it sends fewer packets.
plan_action: Separate bandwidth reduction from power reduction in the cost/performance table. Measure total rail current in both periodic and hybrid modes with identical scan schedules.
test: Measure quiet, contact and fault-mode current at the patch input and regional hub; include quiescent regulators and termination/transceiver activity.
novelty: Event-based low-power sensor networking was established well before this project.

title: Send-on-delta concept: An event-based data reporting strategy
authors: M. Miskowicz
read_scope: Official MDPI static PDF downloaded locally; all15pages49–63 read, including equations1–13, tables1–2, software example and references. Figure3 on p.58 visually inspected.
finding: Separates continuous level-crossing from periodically sampled compound implementations (p.53). Its traffic analysis depends on signal slope, peak density and threshold, and its example compares59 periodic samples with7 events over1.2s at amplitude resolution0.2 (p.58). Heartbeat updates are already described on pp.60–61.
limitation: The analytical comparison assumes a specified signal and resolution; it is not a universal saving, hard latency guarantee or loss/reboot protocol. The sample-count example is a simulation, not a tactile-skin experiment.
plan_action: Adapt to a hybrid:100Hz scanning, delta/contact/fault triggers and fresh absolute snapshots at least every20ms while idle. Include sequence, reboot/session identity and capture time; never treat silence as healthy.
test: Test delta-boundary noise, slow ramps, sustained contacts, burst loss, reboot, timestamp wrap and queue rejection. Keep100Hz worst-case provisioning and measure achieved savings.
novelty: Send-on-delta, compound sampled implementations and added heartbeat updates are all established; this project adapts them.

title: A robust and efficient dynamic network protocol for a large-scale artificial robotic skin
authors: C. Bader, F. Bergner and G. Cheng
read_scope: Repository-indexed abstract, first-page introduction and topology/rerouting figure. Detailed implementation and remaining experiments not read.
finding: Tests a multi-hop skin network with up to204cells. The original abstract reports recovery within50ms and more than30% packet-loss reduction from balancing relative to its previous protocol.
limitation: The supplied2019 review reports40ms and32% greater network size: those are distinct source/metric statements, not interchangeable guarantees. Rerouting requires an intact alternate physical path.
plan_action: Reject literal mesh routing on the single shared CAN bus. Use regional segmentation, bounded failure detection and physical fault containment. Any redundancy needs additional buses/ports and its own BOM.
test: Unplug a node, break a trunk, short the bus and reset the gateway separately. Record the actual affected region and recovery; do not claim single-wirebreak survival from software alone.
novelty: Dynamic robotic-skin routing and load balancing are prior art, but are not functions of the baseline CAN topology.
